translationRepairs: 孫 is kinship, not the surname Sun; since the next unit identifies Meng as Zhang Qian's grandson, the biography heading should use his full name Zhang Meng.
孫 is kinship, not the surname Sun; the heading is naming Zhang Qian's grandson and is clearest in English as Zhang Meng.

Zhang Qian's grandson Sun Meng, styled Ziyou, was a brilliant man who rose to grand counsellor under Emperor Yuan, served on the Xiongnu embassy staff, sat in the inner court, and fell to Shi Xian's slander.

Zhang Qian's grandson Meng, styled Ziyou, was a brilliant man who rose to grand counsellor under Emperor Yuan, served on the Xiongnu embassy staff, sat in the inner court, and fell to Shi Xian's slander.
騫孫猛 is Qian’s grandson Meng; 孫 is kinship, so “Sun Meng” invents a surname. The proposed wording is accurate.
On his return Zhang Qian was appointed grand coachman.
On his return Zhang Qian was appointed Director of Foreign Relations.
大行 is the Han diplomatic office, not 太僕 'grand coachman'; Director of Foreign Relations also matches the established rendering in the parallel Shiji passage.
Army Rectifier Zhao Shi, who had piled up the greatest merit, became grand counsellor of the palace;
Army Rectifier Zhao Shicheng, who had piled up the greatest merit, became grand counsellor of the palace;
軍正趙始成功最多 parses as army rectifier Zhao Shicheng with the most merit; “Zhao Shi” truncates 始成 and misreads 成 with 功.
the army rectifier Zhao Shi had the most merit in success and was made grand counsellor of the palace;
the army rectifier Zhao Shicheng had the most merit and was made grand counsellor of the palace;
趙始成 is the personal name and 功最多 means “had the most merit”; “Zhao Shi” plus “merit in success” mis-segments the Chinese.
Qian returned and was appointed grand coachman.
Qian returned and was appointed Director of Foreign Relations.
大行 is the Han diplomatic office, not the grand coachman; this also aligns the literal field with the established Shiji rendering.
